blockers.title: R3 shareable link contradicts the privacy promise and non-goals
blockers.why: R3 says "Link opens the note for anyone in the workspace" while Scope says notes are "visible only to their author" and non-goals exclude "Sharing private notes with other users in any form", so engineering cannot know which to build.
blockers.fix: Decide whether sharing is in v1; either remove R3 (or move it to a later phase) or rewrite the scope, non-goals and R1 acceptance criteria to allow it.

blockers.title: R4 manager transfer breaks author-only visibility
blockers.why: "When a user is deactivated, their private notes transfer to their manager" exposes notes that authors were told only they could see, which is both a product contradiction and a trust/privacy risk.
blockers.fix: Define the deactivation behavior explicitly (transfer, archive, or delete), tell authors about it in-product, and reconcile it with the scope statement.

blockers.title: Privacy and access rules for private notes are not fully defined
blockers.why: Only exports are raised with Legal; admin access, legal holds, audit logs and API access to "private" notes are not addressed, so the permission model Jo is building has no clear spec.
blockers.fix: Add requirements stating exactly who (admins, support, API, exports) can or cannot access private notes, and get a privacy/security review scheduled with an owner and date.

improvements: Users: expand beyond "Account managers and customer success managers" to say whether other roles can create private notes.
Requirements: add error states (save failures, hitting the 10,000-character limit) and a performance requirement tied to the 1.3 s p95 guardrail.
Success metrics: the survey target depends on "Next quarterly survey"; give a date so the outcome can be judged.
Rollout: add a rollback trigger (e.g., p95 load time above 1.3 s) and a monitoring owner; note support/docs enablement.
Edge cases: specify what happens to private notes when a record is merged or reassigned.
questions: Is sharing a private note with a colleague actually wanted in v1, given the non-goal against sharing in any form?
Should a deactivated user's private notes go to their manager, and will authors be told this up front?
Can workspace admins or support staff ever view private notes, e.g., for legal or compliance requests?
